lesson.menu_title: The Choice You Have Not Made Yet
lesson.menu_desc: Research or teaching -- defending a career decision at eighteen, before you have to make it -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- The Choice You Have Not Made Yet
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Isabel Ladeia Tavares | Lesson 3 -- The Choice You Have Not Made Yet

listenings.text: Everybody warned me off teaching, and I mean everybody. My own supervisor told me I was throwing away a research career, which is a strange thing to say to a twenty-two year old who has not started one yet. So here is what I would say to somebody standing where you are standing. First, nobody is asking you to commit to one life at eighteen. You are choosing what to study for two more years, and that is all you are choosing. Second, if I had picked the research track for the reasons people gave me, I would have been miserable by the second year, because those reasons were all about how the choice looks from outside. And third, and this is the one that surprises people: the two are not opposites. The best teachers I know still read the literature every week, and the best researchers I know are the ones who can explain their own work to a room of seventeen year olds without simplifying it into something false. If you are honestly torn, that is not confusion. That is information.

Good morning, and welcome to the recorded information line for undergraduate progression. This message concerns students who are approaching the point where they choose a track, and it is updated at the start of every semester. The declaration form opens in the first week of March and closes at six in the evening on the last working day of April. Late forms are not accepted, and there is no appeal process for a late form, so please do not leave it to the final afternoon. You are not required to choose one track only. Students who meet the credit requirement may declare both, although you should know that doing both adds between two and three semesters to your degree. If you are unsure, the department strongly recommends two things before you decide. Speak to a student who is already on each track, and sit in on one class from each. Both of those are free, neither of them commits you to anything, and in our experience they change more minds than any document we could send you.
